data.gender_notes: Mahabbah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Rooted in the Arabic language, Mahabbah means 'love' or 'affection'. In Islamic and spiritual traditions, this name symbolizes the deepest and purest form of love, often described as the love between Allah and His creation. The name Mahabbah carries the meaning “Love, Affection” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mahabbah usually hope their child will grow to embody love, affection and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine love in Islam.
data.etymology: Mahabbah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Love, Affection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahabbah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

The name is a constant reminder of the importance of love and kindness, not only towards fellow humans but also towards all living beings.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of Mahabbah is found in the deep connection between love and the divine. In Islamic thought, the love between Allah and His creation is described as the highest form of love. This love is reflected in the human soul, encouraging individuals to seek a deeper connection with their creator. The name Mahabbah is a powerful reminder of this divine and unconditional love, inspiring individuals to strive towards self-betterment, embody compassion, and spread love and kindness in their increasingly complex and interconnected world. Moreover, it serves to strengthen one's faith and evoke a sense of gratefulness towards Allah, making prayer and meditation more meaningful and effective.
